researchQuestion: Close the active-batch backlog aging/cancellation-quality gate and identify what remains unknown about customer concentration.
exactUnresolvedGate: customer concentration plus backlog aging/cancellation quality remain
summary: Primary filings materially close backlog-quality semantics. Vertiv reported $15.0B backlog at December 31, 2025 versus $7.2B a year earlier; the majority was considered firm and expected to ship within 12-18 months. The filing explicitly states orders can be cancelled or rescheduled and that customers can in some circumstances reduce or defer firm backlog, usually with penalties or termination consequences. Q2 2026 primary results show 24% reported sales growth, 18% organic growth and only minor timing shifts tied to supply-chain congestion and multi-phased project execution. This supports backlog as strong demand evidence but not equivalent to guaranteed revenue. Named-customer concentration remains unresolved because current primary filings discuss large-customer bargaining power and demand dependence without disclosing a named-customer revenue table.

evidence.fact: Vertiv estimated combined backlog at $15.0B at December 31, 2025 versus $7.2B at December 31, 2024; the majority was considered firm and expected to ship within 12-18 months.
Orders in backlog may be subject to cancellation or rescheduling; customers have rights in some circumstances, usually with penalties or termination consequences, to reduce or defer firm orders.

Q2 2026 net sales were $3.274B, up 24% year over year, including 18% organic growth; management attributed minor revenue timing shifts primarily to temporary supply-chain congestion and multi-phased project execution.
evidence.sourceLocation: Q2 2026 earnings release furnished with SEC

evidence.fact: At June 30, 2026 Vertiv had $2.811B cash and $300M short-term investments plus $2.484B revolver availability; prior term-loan debt had been fully repaid/refinanced in March 2026.

inference: Backlog quality should be scored as high-demand evidence with an explicit realization haircut, not treated dollar-for-dollar as future revenue, because cancellation/rescheduling rights are contractually present and acquired-company contracts may have differing termination terms.

The doubling of backlog plus strong Q2 organic sales growth argues against a near-term demand-collapse interpretation, while the 12-18 month fulfillment horizon creates execution, pricing-lag and cancellation exposure that should remain visible in risk/confidence.
unknowns: Named-customer concentration and exact percentage exposure to top hyperscalers remain undisclosed in the reviewed current primary filings.
No public primary table was found that ages the $15.0B backlog into finer quarterly buckets or quantifies historical cancellation rates.
Acquisition-added backlog may have heterogeneous cancellation terms; exact mix is not disclosed.
falsifiers: A later filing showing substantial cancellations, deferrals or backlog contraction without offsetting deliveries.
A primary disclosure revealing materially higher single-customer dependence than current qualitative risk language implies.
